title: Sparrow quant field notes — weekly research capture
content:
WEEKLY RESEARCH CAPTURE — 'SPARROW' QUANT PROBE
Date: 2027-11-02
Authors: Priya Nambiar (owner), Ethan Morales, Lina Zhou

Summary:
- This week's focus: narrow-scope probe of 4-bit KV quantization + per-channel symmetric weights (KV4-sym) on Sparrow-7B variant used for internal LLM-onboarding. Goal: measure regression surface (perplexity + downstream QA accuracy) and runtime impact under our continuous-batching runtime.
- Quick verdict: KV4-sym + microbatching gives 35% reduction in GPU memory, ~1.25x throughput improvement when sequence lengths <512, and median latency improvements of ~12ms (p50) vs baseline fp16 in our continuous-batching config. Small but measurable QA drop (EM -1.6 points on SQuAD-mini), largely concentrated on long-context QA.

Experiment matrix (running in dev cluster 'sparrow-lab'):
- Models: sparrow-7b-v1 (fp16 baseline), sparrow-7b-kv4-sym (quantized), sparrow-7b-kv4-asym (control)
- HW: A100-40GB (dedicated dev), batch config: continuous batching with target latency SLO 80ms
- Seq lengths: 128 / 256 / 1024 (edge case)
- Metrics collected: lm-perplexity (subsample), EM/LEX accuracy on SQuAD-mini, tokens/sec, GPU mem (MB), p50/p95 latency

Key results (aggregated):
- fp16 baseline (seq256): tokens/sec 1,720 | GPU mem 14,200MB | p50 36ms | p95 92ms
- kv4-sym (seq256): tokens/sec 2,160 | GPU mem 9,200MB | p50 24ms | p95 84ms | SQuAD-mini EM -1.6
- kv4-asym (seq256): tokens/sec 2,060 | GPU mem 9,600MB | p50 26ms | p95 88ms | SQuAD-mini EM -2.4
- seq1024: quantization regressions magnify; kv4-sym EM -3.8 vs baseline and p95 spikes due to KV cache thrashing in runtime (need better cache retention policy)

Observations:
- Per-channel symmetric quantization produced slightly better accuracy vs asymmetric in these runs — hypothesis: symmetric weights reduce outlier scaling variance for attention keys.
- The runtime's KV cache prefetch + microbatching interplay looks promising: for short sequences (<512) we get throughput gains without hurting p95; for long sequences (>768) the runtime currently serializes cache refill in a way that increases p95.
- Memory wins are significant for Dedicated offerings (predictable capacity). For Private on-prem small GPU fleets this could enable more concurrent replicas.

Open engineering tasks (owner initials):
- PRI-1: Add a fast path in runtime for kv4-sym that avoids dequantizing full KV pages on read. (Priya)
- PRI-2: Add a telemetry tag on cache-evictions to trace which request sizes cause early eviction (Ethan)
- PRI-3: Run a larger SQuAD+NQ sweep across 25 seeds to better characterize variance (Lina)
- PRI-4: Add an integration test in model-onboarding flow to fail if EM drop >3.0 on SQuAD-mini (Marco)

Meeting notes (2027-11-02 weekly applied-ml sync):
- Lina: showed visual of per-layer activation ranges; layer 20/21 have larger outliers which map to attention heads sensitive to quantization.
- Marco: surfaced a customer onboarding ticket (CUST-884) where model did not fit into 2xT4s; suggested recommending dedicated with kv4-sym frontend to customers as stopgap.
- Ethan: proposed a new microbatch heuristic: if SLO <50ms, prefer shallow microbatch pipeline (max-batches=2) to reduce p95 tail from cache refill.

Decisions / next steps:
- Prototype runtime fast path for kv4-sym reads (Priya) and schedule a perf run next Tue (2027-11-09).
- Add eviction telemetry and a quick dashboard (Ethan) for immediate triaging.
- Run larger offline eval to confirm SQuAD variance (Lina) — target complete by 2027-11-10.

Notes to self:
- Consider comparing to 3-bit experiments but only after addressing numeric stability in layernorm (we saw NaNs in earlier runs).
- Link to PR with current quantization encoder changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145
- Related confluence: Quantization Playbook (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AMP/Quantization+Playbook)

Quick links / tickets:
- ENG-1429: kv4-sym runtime fast-path
- CUST-884: onboarding capacity failure (sales flagged)

Appendix (raw numbers dump):
- run-101 (fp16, seq256): avg_tokens_sec 1720 | gpu_mem 14200MB | p50 36 | p95 92
- run-102 (kv4-sym, seq256): avg_tokens_sec 2160 | gpu_mem 9200MB | p50 24 | p95 84 | SQuAD-mini EM 67.4 (baseline 69.0)
- run-109 (kv4-sym, seq1024): tokens_sec 1180 | gpu_mem 11300MB | p50 154 | p95 420 | EM 65.2

End.
